root_cause.text: `xe_sync_entry_parse()` in the DRM xe sync subsystem had error paths after allocating `syncobj`/`fence`/`chain_fence`/user-fence references that returned immediately without calling `xe_sync_entry_cleanup()`, leaving partially initialized `xe_sync_entry` state and leaking references.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes multiple `return -EINVAL`, `return -ENOMEM`, and `return err` sites in `drivers/gpu/drm/xe/xe_sync.c` to `goto free_sync`, then adds `free_sync: xe_sync_entry_cleanup(sync); return err;`, and the commit message explicitly says “Several of those paths returned directly, leaving partially initialized state and leaking refs.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix sync entry parsing to clean up allocated state when fence acquisition fails.
intent_record.what: In `xe_sync_entry_parse()`, the code handling a missing `signal` now changes the error path after `drm_syncobj_fence_get(sync->syncobj)` returns `NULL`: instead of immediately returning `-EINVAL`, it assigns `-EINVAL` to `err` and jumps to the `free_sync` cleanup label.
intent_record.how: Behaviorally, this preserves the existing error result but routes failure through the function's cleanup path, ensuring any resources associated with the partially parsed sync entry are released before the function exits.

intent_record.intent_summary: Route sync parsing failures through shared cleanup to avoid leaking partially initialized state.
intent_record.what: The function changed two early-return error paths into a shared cleanup path: when `dma_fence_chain_alloc()` fails, it now sets `err = -ENOMEM` and jumps to `free_sync`; when `drm_syncobj_fence_get()` returns no fence, it now sets `err = -EINVAL` and jumps to `free_sync`; and when `dma_fence_chain_find_seqno()` returns an error, it now also jumps to `free_sync` instead of returning immediately.
intent_record.how: At runtime, failures during sync entry parsing now funnel through a common cleanup label rather than exiting immediately, ensuring any partially initialized `sync` state is released before the error is reported. This prevents resource leaks or inconsistent cleanup on allocation/lookup/sequence-number errors while preserving the same error codes.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add cleanup on parse failure so partially initialized sync entries are released before returning an error.
intent_record.what: A new error-handling label `free_sync:` was added at the end of `xe_sync_entry_parse()`, which calls `xe_sync_entry_cleanup(sync);` and returns `err` before the function exits.
intent_record.how: If `xe_sync_entry_parse()` fails after partially initializing `sync`, it now cleans up that partially constructed state before returning the error, preventing resource leaks or leftover inconsistent state.

grouping_result.intent: Add cleanup on parse failure so partially initialized sync entries are released before returning an error.

consistency_review.core_intent: Add cleanup on sync entry parse failure so partially initialized state is released before returning an error.

relevance_review.reason: The changes directly match the root cause: they add cleanup in xe_sync_entry_parse() error paths so partially initialized sync entry state and allocated references are released instead of leaking.

candidates.rationale: This immediate return on fence acquisition failure exits `xe_sync_entry_parse()` without invoking cleanup, leaving any previously allocated syncobj/fence state in the partially initialized `xe_sync_entry` leaked.
This early return when `dma_fence_chain_alloc()` fails bypasses `xe_sync_entry_cleanup()`, so any earlier allocations or references associated with the sync entry may remain unreleased.
This error path returns immediately after `drm_syncobj_fence_get()` fails, which is the exact pattern causing partial initialization to escape cleanup and leak references.
This return on `dma_fence_chain_find_seqno()` failure propagates an error without cleanup, matching the root cause of leaving a partially initialized sync entry and leaking acquired resources.

vuln_statements.explanation: This immediate return after `drm_syncobj_fence_get()` fails exits `xe_sync_entry_parse()` without calling `xe_sync_entry_cleanup()`, which matches the root cause of leaving a partially initialized `xe_sync_entry` and leaking acquired references.
This return on `dma_fence_chain_alloc()` failure bypasses shared cleanup, so any earlier allocated syncobj/fence/chain_fence state in the partially initialized entry can be leaked.
This propagation of `dma_fence_chain_find_seqno()` errors exits without cleanup, leaving previously acquired resources referenced by the partially initialized sync entry.
